fields.value: Design training recovery across interruptible GPU rentals

Jack Heart requested this investigation on 2026-11-05 after Manabot MTG-249 lost a Vast GPU during training. Design training workflows and public Etude SDK interfaces robust to interruptible/ephemeral GPU compute. Deliver a concrete design and implementation plan; broad implementation and paid trials are not selected by this capture.

Problem: MTG-249 run e51f61b92931 at source af601877e and Etude lock 64e9eaabf016f567cb9567280bcf8730f6f5d524 ended lost/machine_lost at 2026-11-05 13:09:07 UTC, with no final output inventory or exit code, well before its rental deadline. Three learners completed 256 updates/65,536 games each; the fourth's last receipt had 83 updates. 36 manually backed-up artifacts (371,853,657 bytes) preserve at least 217,856 games; no evaluation endpoints survived because evaluation followed all eight learners. Rental absence was confirmed; about $2.64 whole-rental cost. Cause is unknown: do not assert spot preemption, OOM, or host fault. Vast has on-demand and interruptible offerings; record actual acquisition mode and distinguish pause/preemption, host disappearance, lease expiry and learner failure.

Desired outcome: a researcher can run long training on disposable GPUs without depending on one machine surviving to final upload. Recovery is explicit, bounded, scientifically honest and supported through Etude's ordinary API, not task-specific SSH backup scripts.

Investigate and recommend: durable incremental artifact/checkpoint publication with atomic manifests, hashes and acknowledged durability; restart boundaries and lineage across attempts/machines; per-learner/seed jobs and evaluation delivery as alternatives to one monolithic cohort; graceful notification handling and abrupt loss with no notice; controller restart and uncertain acquisition reconciliation; a single cumulative budget and deadline including retries, transfer, idle time and teardown; retry bounds and unsupported/incompatible-state refusal.

Define the Etude/learner boundary. Etude owns acquisition, delivery, attempt lineage and scheduling; the application declares restorable state and continuation semantics. State may include model, optimizer, EMA, schedules, RNG, sampler/environment state and absolute update/exposure counters. Exact continuation differs from fresh streams or warm-start with optimizer resets: require declared discontinuities, never silently infer equivalence from weights. Preserve completed work and immutable failed attempts without selecting by score or claiming partial cohorts are complete.

Acceptance: one reviewed design with Python API examples, responsibility/sequence diagrams and recovery semantics; demonstrate through controlled fault-injection fixtures loss before/after checkpoint commit, partial upload, stale/duplicate completion, controller restart and reacquisition. Verify only durable state is resumed, completed units are not duplicated, scientific identities/counters stay meaningful, and original budget/deadline still cap total execution. Explain bounded lost work and publication costs; no artificial load/stress tests. Include migration/adoption path for Manabot while keeping provider-neutral design. No paid compute authority transfers from MTG-249; that Task's original $25 remains separate.

Evidence references (copy needed contents into this Task checkout before execution): Manabot experiments/protocols/state-representation-5da5f4-gpu.md; manifest-backed experiments/data/state-representation-gpu-5da5f4/batched-plateau/terminal-20261105T130907Z/; scratch/vast-host-diagnosis.md. MTG-249: loopflow://manabot/task/MTG-249. Public rental types: [https://vast.ai/article/Rental-Types](<https://vast.ai/article/Rental-Types>).

Overlap: EXP-8 covers unhealthy inference workers and avoiding duplicate work; reuse its ownership/reconciliation ideas but this Task owns durable training continuation. EXP-12 owns launcher database migrations; EXP-13 uncertain owned-SSH create replies; EXP-17 large-output transfer threading. Open PR59 (MTG-175 branch jack/mtg175-output-delivery) changes src/etude/launch/worker/courier.py for bounded parallel final uploads, not periodic recovery state; coordinate rather than replace it: [https://github.com/loopflowstudio/etude/pull/59](<https://github.com/loopflowstudio/etude/pull/59>). PR56 (MTG-175 evaluation queue) queues checkpoint eval jobs behind capacity: [https://github.com/loopflowstudio/etude/pull/56](<https://github.com/loopflowstudio/etude/pull/56>). PR58 covers report metrics/checkpoint planning. Preserve choices reserved to their owners.
